title: Speed vs velocity: why direction matters
examples: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
Can you accelerate at a steady speed?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Velocity is speed plus a direction

explain.say: Imagine two taxis in Mumbai, both doing 40 kilometres per hour. One drives north, one drives south. Are they doing the same thing? Their speed is the same, but their velocity is not. Let us find out why.

explain.say: Look at the left card: speed. Speed only tells you how fast. 40 kilometres per hour is a speed. It is a scalar, which means it has a size but no direction. Can you think of something else with a size but no direction?

draw.verdict: Velocity is speed plus a direction

explain.say: Like your mass or the temperature, nice! Now the right card: velocity. Velocity is speed in a stated direction, like 40 kilometres per hour north. It is a vector, which means a size and a direction. Which taxi has a velocity of 40 north?

draw.verdict: Velocity is speed plus a direction

explain.say: The first one, yes! Now a clever bit. Run round a track at a steady speed: your speed stays the same, but your direction keeps turning. So your velocity keeps changing, and you are accelerating even at steady speed. Strange, but true!

explain.say: Great thinking! Wow fact: the Moon races round Earth at about 1 kilometre per second. Its speed hardly changes, yet its velocity changes every moment as it curves. Challenge: run one full lap and finish at the start. What is your average velocity?

faq.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
faq.a: Speed tells you how fast something moves. Velocity tells you how fast and in which direction.
asks: Are speed and velocity the same?

faq.a: A scalar is a quantity with only a size, like speed, mass, distance or temperature.
A vector is a quantity with a size and a direction, like velocity, force or displacement. We often draw vectors as arrows.

faq.q: Can you accelerate at a steady speed?
faq.a: Yes. Acceleration is any change in velocity, and turning changes your direction. So going round a bend at steady speed is still accelerating.
Yes. A minus sign just means the opposite direction to the one you chose as positive, such as moving left instead of right.

facts: Velocity is a vector; speed is a scalar.
The Moon orbits Earth at about 1 kilometre per second.

quiz.say: Which of these is a velocity?
quiz.show: Which of these is a velocity?

options.say: 15 metres per second to the east

quiz.why: A velocity needs a speed and a direction, like 15 metres per second east.

wrong.1: That has no direction, so it is a speed.
wrong.2: That is a distance with a direction, called a displacement, not a velocity.

quiz.say: You run one lap and finish where you started. Your average velocity is…
quiz.show: You run one lap and finish where you started. Your average velocity is…

options.show: The same as your average speed
options.say: The same as your average speed

quiz.why: You end up where you began, so your overall displacement and average velocity are zero.

wrong.0: Speed uses total distance; velocity uses how far you end up from the start, which is zero.
wrong.2: Velocity is only negative if you end up on the opposite side of the start.
